newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures were boosted on Friday by non-resident buying and shrugged off a decline in the U.S. unemployment rate to 4.9 percent, surprising some economists who expected a strong negative reaction.
Analysts were also perplexed by the fact the French market was still not pricing in the risk of a Socialist win in the May 25/June 1 parliamentary election.
Traders, however, were optimistic and said while the upcoming election and the U.S. central bank's policy meeting on May 20 could slow gains, the contract looked set to head back to 130.

"Basically as an economist I do not understand how markets could react so positively to an unemployment rate at 4.9 percent," Eric Chaney, economist at Morgan Stanley in Paris said. "I'm also surprised the French market is so complacent about the election. The most likely outcome is a Chirac win, but its not 100 percent."
The U.S. economy created a smaller-than-expected 142,000 non-farm jobs in April, but the unemployment rate fell to 4.9 percent from 5.2 percent, its lowest level since the 1970s.
The June bond contract ended the week at 129.48, higher than when the U.S. jobs report was released.

Chaney said there was little new in the French Socialists' electoral programme released on Friday and while their policies would be negative for the bond market "no risk premium appears to have been priced in".
An economist at a French bank agreed, saying a Socialist win would be disastrous for the French market. He said they were recommending their clients sell French interest rate futures.

June PIBOR came under pressure immediately before and after the snap election was called by President Jacques Chirac on April 21 but has since stabilised. It was unchanged at 96.42 on Friday, up from a low of 96.26 a week earlier.

Still a trader said the French bond market was "very strong again". He said the market was ripe for some consolidation, perhaps back to 129.16, closing the gap left Friday morning, but any dips would attract buyers.

The rally in the bond future on Friday, driven initially by a French brokerage buying for a U.S. fund, helped the Treasury offload another three billion francs of OATs as primary dealers have the right to buy some bonds at the average price at Wednesday's auction.
It sold a total of 25.26 billion francs of bonds, yet again above its target, which was 21-23 billion francs this month.
The franc was up slightly against the mark at 3.3720 compared with 3.3730 late on Thursday and a low of 3.3785 last week.

Two opinion polls were expected during the weekend. An IFOP poll for Le Journal du Dimanche was scheduled for release on Saturday and a Sofres poll in Le Figaro was expected to be published late on Sunday.
